To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the oxidation of fatty acids is reduced and the content of fatty acid-binding protein and hormone-sensitive lipase is increased in the skeletal muscle of aging rats.
the oxidation of fatty acids by skeletal muscle is reduced in middle-aged and old adult rats, and that this reduction is associated with an accumulation of muscle triglycerides.

in the absence of hyperglycemia and hyperinsulinemia, the utilization of palmitate by skeletal muscle of aging animals is impaired and that this impairment may contribute to the increased muscle TG accumulation observed in aging animals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanisms of impaired glucose tolerance and insulin resistance in aging rats.
the effects of aging on the regulation of fatty acid metabolism in skeletal muscle.
the role of the insulin-like growth factors in the regulation of glucose homeostasis and the mechanisms of insulin resistance during aging.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the reduction in fatty acid oxidation and the accumulation of triglyceride in muscle are important factors in age-related insulin resistance.
aging impairs FA metabolism in muscle, and this impairment is associated with a decrease in FA oxidation, an accumulation of TG in red and white muscle, and a decrease in HSL activity in red muscle.
aging rats are less efficient at oxidizing fatty acids in skeletal muscle.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, under basal (low insulin) conditions, there is an age-related decline in FA oxidation in skeletal muscle.
aging is associated with a decrease in FA oxidation and an increase in FA esterification in muscle.

the age-related changes in FA metabolism are not a direct consequence of a decline in insulin action, and that the age-related decline in FA oxidation is likely due to a decrease in FA uptake by muscle.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the utilization of fatty acid as fuel by skeletal muscle is impaired in the aging rat.
the accumulation of TG is associated with the reduction of FA utilization and the decrease of HSL content in the muscle of aging rats.
the accumulation of TG is not only associated with the aging process but also with the reduction of FA oxidation and HSL content.
